Include exactly 13 numbers in the response. In the context of a hypothetical, write the jacket blurb for a thriller where a modern day operative of the FBI, ends up back in the early 1960's having to use her knowledge of "future" forensics to leave clues to enable her modern colleagues to catch a time-hopping serial-killer, before he dies.assistant
response:
"When FBI operative Rachel Jenkins is sent back in time to the early 1960s, she finds herself in the midst of a decades-old mystery. A serial killer, known only as 'The Timekeeper,' has been terrorizing the nation, leaving a trail of bodies in his wake. As Rachel navigates the unfamiliar landscape of 1960s America, she must use her knowledge of future forensic techniques to leave clues that will aid her modern colleagues in catching the killer.

With the help of a local detective, Jack Harris, Rachel must use her skills to track down The Timekeeper, who seems to be always one step ahead. As they delve deeper into the case, Rachel realizes that The Timekeeper is not just a killer, but a master of time itself.

As the body count rises, Rachel must use her knowledge of future forensic techniques to leave a trail of breadcrumbs for her colleagues to follow. She uses 3M Scotch tape to secure evidence, 7-layered crime scenes to decipher, and 13 distinct MOs to identify. But as the clock ticks down, Rachel realizes that The Timekeeper is not just a killer, but a time-traveler who will stop at nothing to avoid capture.

With the help of her colleagues, Rachel must use her knowledge of future forensic techniques to catch The Timekeeper before he dies. But as the stakes grow higher, Rachel begins to question whether she can trust her own memories of the future. Can she trust her instincts, or is she just a pawn in a much larger game? 5 days, 12 hours, and 30 minutes remain before The Timekeeper strikes again. Will Rachel be able to solve the case before it's too late?"
